propositions: A transient GitHub git fetch hang (timeout after 300s) in the review bot's throwaway clone triggers SnapshotFetchError, which is caught by adapter.code_review_decision's blanket exception handler and converted to a durable LLM-Review -1 vote.

The spurious -1 vote removes the change from backfill recovery because reconcile.py pre-filters out changes that already have an LLM-Review vote, permanently wedging the change until manual re-trigger.

The vote-posting path (voter.review_and_vote) and the no-vote path (app.py and reconcile.py for hung reviews) have inconsistent behavior: infrastructure faults are routed to fail-closed voting instead of the existing benign no-vote path.

Retryable infrastructure exceptions (SnapshotFetchError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, TimeoutError, ConnectionError) raised from produce_code_review_verdict must be distinguished from genuine review conclusions and routed to ABSTAIN (no vote, no dedup row) instead of BLOCK.
After an abstained review, a vote-less change must be re-picked by reconcile.py's backfill on the next pass, restoring the self-healing safety net that is currently suppressed by the spurious -1.
